newsitem.title: UK: Brunner Mond valuation set at 130-150 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Brunner Mond valuation set at 130-150 mln stg.

text.p: British soda ash producer Brunner Mond Plc set itself a valuation range of between 130 and 150 million pounds on Monday for its planned flotation on the London Stock Exchange later this month.
Brunner Mond, which merged with three other businesses to form chemicals giant Imperial Chemicals Industries Plc in 1926, was acquired by a management buyout team in 1991.
The company said in a statement the valuation reflects an offer price range of between 170 and 210 pence per share, and the offer is expected to raise up to 46.0 million pounds net of expenses.
A company spokesman said the offer "is being priced as expected and on an attractive basis."
Brunner Mond said the mid-range offer price of 190 pence represents a price/earnings multiple of 11.2 times its pro forma earnings per share of 16.9 pence for the year ended June 30.
On the same basis the mid-range price would imply a gross dividend yield of 5.6 percent, based on a notional net dividend for the year of 8.45 pence.
Brunner Mond is the U.K.'s only producer of soda ash, used in the manufacture of glass, chemicals and detergents. It also makes sodium bicarbonate, used in some foods and pharmaceuticals.

Chief executive David Wertheim said the outlook for the group is "better than it has been for several years. This is underpinned by favourable new contracts, improved soda ash prices and strong demand."
Bookbuilding in the stock is already underway, with the announcement of the offer price and share allocation expected on Sept 19. Dealing in the shares is due to begin on Sept 26.
